en: The Ritual Manual for the Practice of the Great Compassionate Heart Mantra of the Thousand Hands and Thousand Eyes,
originally compiled by the Venerable Zhi Li of the Four Illuminations (Siming),
with texts revised and recompiled by the Vinaya Master Du Ti of Mount Hua.
Shramana Jixian of Jiahe supplements the image and compares the woodblocks for printing.
*Namo* to the Greatly Compassionate Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva (recited three times).
All with utmost reverence.
With single-minded devotion, prostrate to the eternally abiding Triple Gem of the ten directions.
(After the first prostration is completed, the leader chants:
"All these members of the assembly, each kneeling with palms joined, reverently hold incense and flowers."
Through this Dharma-offering, may these clouds of incense and flowers pervade the worlds of the ten directions;
may each and every Buddha-field be adorned with immeasurable fragrances, fulfilling the path of the Bodhisattvas and accomplishing the fragrance of the Tathāgata. (Recite as follows:)
These fragrant flowers of mine pervade the ten directions, forming subtle and wondrous platforms of light;
there are celestial music and divine precious incense, celestial delicacies and divine precious robes—
these inconceivable particles of the sublime Dharma, from each single particle emerge all other particles.
From every single atom emerge all phenomena, revolving without obstruction, mutually adorning one another, reaching everywhere before the Triple Gem in the ten directions.
Before the Triple Gem throughout the dharma-realm of the ten directions, there is my own body everywhere performing offerings;
each and every one of these pervades the entire dharma-realm.
In each and every place, without confusion or obstruction, they perform Buddha-works throughout the limits of the future;
universally perfuming all sentient beings within the Dharma-realm, those who receive this perfuming all resolve upon Bodhicitta and together enter the non-arising state to realize Buddha-wisdom.
Having completed the offerings, with all due reverence (chanting once and prostrating):
Homage to the Tathāgata Dharmaprabhāsa of the past and to the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara appearing before us, who has perfected wondrous merit.

Possessing great compassion, within a single body and mind, he manifests a thousand hands and eyes to illuminate and perceive the Dharma-realm, protecting and sustaining all sentient beings and causing them to give rise to the vast mind of enlightenment.
He teaches them to uphold the perfect and divine mantra so that they may forever leave the evil realms behind and be reborn before the Buddhas.
Even those with grave offenses of the Avīci Hell or those afflicted by malignant diseases for which no remedy can be found—he causes all such things to be completely eliminated.
His eloquence is profound; whatever vows and aspirations one makes in this life shall all be fulfilled, without any doubt.

He can cause one to swiftly attain the three vehicles and quickly ascend to the stage of Buddhahood. His majestic spiritual power is beyond the reach of praise. Therefore, with a single mind, I take refuge in him and pay homage to him with my head.
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to the World-Honored One, our Original Teacher Śākyamuni. (Visualize and recite:
"The nature of both the one who prostrates and the object of prostration is empty and tranquil; The resonance between the response and the invocation is inconceivable.
This place of my practice is like a celestial jewel, Within which the shadow-forms of Śākyamuni Tathāgata appear."
My own form appears before Śākyamuni; With head touching his feet, I take refuge and pay homage.
(As when paying homage to Amitābha Buddha, one says: "The image of Amitābha Buddha appears... and so forth. When paying homage to the Sangha, simply change "Bodhisattvas" etc. for "the Sangha";
hereafter, follow this pattern according to the respective positions.)
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the World-Honored One Amitābha of the Western World of Ultimate Bliss;
with single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the World-Honored One King of Thousand Rays Abiding in Tranquility of immeasurable billions of kalpas past;
with single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, as numerous as the sands of ninety-nine billion Gaṅgā Rivers in the past.
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to the World-Honored One, Dharmaprabhāsa, of immeasurable kalpas past;
with single-minded devotion, I prostrate to all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, of the ten directions;
with single-minded devotion, I prostrate to the thousand Buddhas of the Bhadrakalpa and to all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, of the three periods of time.
(The assembly hears the bell and offers incense.
With single-minded devotion, prostrate to the Great Dharani of the Wondrous Phrases of the Vast, Perfect, and Unobstructed Great Compassionate Mind.
(Recite three times and prostrate three times; visualize as follows:)
The Dharma-nature of true emptiness is like space; The eternally abiding Dharma-treasure is inconceivable.
My own body’s shadow appears before this Dharma-treasure; With single-minded devotion, I take refuge and pay homage according to the Dharma.
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to all the *dhāraṇīs* spoken by Avalokiteśvara, as well as to all the Honored Ones of the ten directions and the three periods of time.
[The Assembly Offers Incense] With single-minded devotion,
we pay homage to the Greatly Compassionate and Benevolent Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara of a Thousand Hands and a Thousand Eyes.
[Recite the name of the Bodhisattva] three times and perform three prostrations, while contemplating:
"The nature of both the one who pays homage and the object of homage is empty and quiescent; the resonance between the path and its response is inconceivable.
My place of practice is like a jewel of Indra, within which the reflections of the Great Compassionate Bodhisattvas appear."
I manifest my body before the Great Compassionate One, seeking to extinguish hindrances and prostrating at his feet.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Dhāraṇīśvara-rāja.
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas Sūryaprabha and Candraprabha;
with single-minded devotion, I prostrate to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas Ratnarāja, Bhaiṣajyarāja, and Bhaiṣajyasamudgata;
with single-minded devotion, I prostrate to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas Avataṃsaka, Mahāvyūha, and Ratnagarbha.
With single-minded devotion, prostrate to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas Guṇakara, Vajragarbha, and Gaganagañja.
As the Sūtra says: "If there be bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, or boys and girls who desire..."
Those who recite and uphold [this practice] should first give rise to a mind of compassion toward all sentient beings and make this vow before me.
(The assembly follows by raising [the prayer]; hereafter, strike the chime once for each character).
Homage to the Greatly Compassionate Avalokiteśvara; May I quickly understand all dharmas.
Homage to the Greatly Compassionate Avalokiteśvara; May I soon attain the eye of wisdom.
Homage to the Greatly Compassionate Avalokiteśvara; May I swiftly deliver all sentient beings.
Homage to the Greatly Compassionate Avalokiteśvara; May I quickly attain skillful means.
Homage to the Greatly Compassionate Avalokiteśvara; May I swiftly board the ship of Prajñā.
Homage to the Greatly Compassionate Avalokiteśvara; May I quickly cross over the sea of suffering.
Homage to the Greatly Compassionate Avalokiteśvara! May I swiftly attain the path of precepts and concentration.
Homage to the Greatly Compassionate Avalokiteśvara! May I soon ascend the mountain of Nirvāṇa.
Homage to the Greatly Compassionate Avalokiteśvara! May I quickly reach the abode of the unconditioned.
Homage to the Greatly Compassionate Avalokiteśvara! May I soon become one with the Dharmatā-body.
If I face the Mountain of Knives, the mountain shall collapse of its own accord;
If I face the Cauldron of Fire, the cauldron shall dry up of its own accord.
If I head toward hell, hell itself shall vanish;
If I head toward the hungry ghosts, the hungry ghosts shall be satiated;
If I head toward the asuras, their evil minds shall be naturally subdued.
If I am reborn among the animals, may I spontaneously attain great wisdom.

(The practitioner visualizes themselves before these Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, reciting their honored names with utmost sincerity and urgency, as if they were on the verge of being burned or drowned and seeking rescue.)
Homage to Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva. Homage to Amitābha Buddha.

(Recite each ten times with a slightly rapid pace. At the fourth and seventh recitations, raise the final syllable of the opening phrase; throughout, ring the large bell loudly. At the conclusion of the Buddha’s name, strike once to conclude, prostrate, rise, and inquire after one another. The presiding master raises [the incense]).

The Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One, if sentient beings who recite and uphold this Great Compassionate Divine Mantra should fall into the three evil realms, I vow not to attain perfect enlightenment.
If those who recite and uphold this Great Compassionate Divine Mantra should not be reborn in the lands of the Buddhas, I vow not to attain perfect enlightenment.
If those who recite and uphold this Great Compassionate Divine Mantra should not obtain [the state of] non-..."

Regarding the measure of my samādhi and eloquence: I vow that I shall not attain perfect awakening if, while reciting and upholding this Great Compassionate Divine Mantra, any of my requests in this present life do not reach fulfillment;
were this to happen, it could not be called the Dharani of the Great Compassionate Heart.
Having spoken these words, he stood before the assembled multitude with palms joined, directing his attention toward all sentient beings.

Giving rise to a heart of great compassion, with a face opened in a smiling countenance, he then spoke these wondrous verses of the Great Dharani of the Vast, Perfect, and Unobstructed Heart of Great Compassion. The Dharani says:

2) Vadyaye (83) Svāhā (84). When the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara had finished speaking this mantra, the great earth shook in six ways, and the heavens rained down a profusion of precious flowers.
All the Buddhas of the ten directions were filled with joy, while the heavenly Māras and non-Buddhist practitioners were struck with terror, their hair standing on end. One.

The entire assembly all attained the realization of the fruits: some attained the fruit of *srotāpanna*, some attained the fruit of *sakṛdāgāmin*, some attained the fruit of *anāgāmin*, and some attained the fruit of *arhat*.
Some attained the first bhūmi, the second, third, fourth, fifth, and even up to the tenth bhūmi. Immeasurable sentient beings resolved their minds upon Bodhi. (One prostration with silent recitation)
I and all sentient beings have, since beginningless time, been constantly obstructed by the heavy offenses of the three karmas and six sense faculties.

Consequently, we have not seen the Buddhas, do not know the essential way of escape, and merely follow the cycle of birth and death, remaining ignorant of the sublime principle. Although I now understand it, I am still [bound] together with sentient beings.

We are all equally obstructed by various grave offenses. Now, before Avalokiteśvara and the Buddhas of the ten directions, we universally repent on behalf of all sentient beings, taking refuge and confessing our transgressions.
We pray only that you will grant your protection and cause these obstructions to be extinguished. Having finished this recitation, kneel and chant as follows:

For the sake of all sentient beings within the Dharma-realm of the four debts of gratitude and the three realms of existence, I vow that they shall all sever and eliminate the three obstructions. I take refuge and repent.
(Having chanted this, prostrate with the five limbs touching the ground, and further reflect in the mind:)
From beginningless time until now, I and all sentient beings, due to craving and false views, have internally conceived a self and persons and externally associated with evil friends;

we have failed to rejoice in even a hair’s breadth of another’s virtue, but rather, throughout our three karmic doors, have extensively committed manifold transgressions. Although these acts were not on a vast scale, [the resulting suffering is immense].
Evil thoughts pervaded his mind, continuing day and night without interruption. He concealed his transgressions and did not wish for others to know them;

he feared neither the evil realms nor the loss of face, lacking both gradual progress and shame. Having denied the existence of cause and effect, he has today come to have deep faith in cause and effect.
One gives rise to profound shame and remorse; one gives rise to great dread; one discloses and repents; one severs the continuity of [unwholesome] thoughts;

one generates the bodhicitta; one abandons evil and cultivates good; one diligently exerts the three karmas; one overturns former grave transgressions; and one rejoices in even a hair’s breadth of merit belonging to ordinary beings or sages.

I call to mind the Buddhas of the ten directions, who possess great merit and wisdom, and are able to rescue and deliver myself and all sentient beings from the sea of the two deaths, placing us upon the shore of the three virtues.
Since beginningless time, I have failed to realize that the intrinsic nature of all phenomena is empty and quiescent, and have extensively committed various evils.
Now I realize emptiness and stillness. For the sake of seeking Bodhi and for the sake of all sentient beings, I shall extensively cultivate all virtues and universally sever all evils.
I only pray that Avalokiteśvara will compassionately accept me. (Having finished the visualization, kneel and recite:)
With a sincere heart, we, the disciples [Name] and others, together with all sentient beings of the Dharma-realm, now focus our minds as one.

The fundamental nature is endowed with the thousand dharmas, each possessing spiritual power and the clarity of wisdom. Above, this is equal to the Buddha-mind; below, it pervades all conscious beings.

Since beginningless time, the movement of darkness has obstructed this tranquil clarity. In every encounter, we are deluded and confused; in every thought, we are bound and attached. Within the state of universal equality, we give rise to...
